statement: On a normal die, opposite faces add up to 7. Three dice lie on a table. Their top faces show 2, 4 and 5. What is the total of their three bottom faces?

choices.misconception: I added the top faces, $2 + 4 + 5 = 11$, instead of the faces underneath.
I thought opposite faces add up to 8, so I found $6 + 4 + 3 = 13$.
I thought the bottom face shows the next number after the top, so I added $3 + 5 + 6 = 14$.
I added 7 for each die, $3 \times 7 = 21$, and forgot to take away the top faces.

hints: Each bottom face is opposite one top face.
Opposite faces make 7, so each bottom face is 7 take away its top face. You can find the three bottoms one at a time, or use the total of all six faces at once.
The bottoms are $7 - 2 = 5$, $7 - 4 = 3$ and $7 - 5 = 2$. Add these three numbers.

solutions.reliable: Work die by die. Under the 2 is $7 - 2 = 5$, under the 4 is $7 - 4 = 3$, under the 5 is $7 - 5 = 2$. The bottoms add to $5 + 3 + 2 = 10$. The transferable idea: on a die, knowing one face tells you the face opposite it.
solutions.elegant: Each die's top and bottom add to 7, so the three tops and three bottoms together make $3 \times 7 = 21$. The tops make 11, so the bottoms make $21 - 11 = 10$.

whyOnTest: Dice questions on the test lean on one fact, opposite faces add to 7, and reward using it as a total rather than one face at a time.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
